name: Audit the evidence that updates authority
human: When a system gains permission through your behavior, inspect whether its way of helping changed that evidence.
agent: Authenticate the grant; replay the exact rule; estimate or bound the total intervention-policy contrast in typed future scope; return governance judgment separately.

name: Specify the terms of chosen change
human: People can choose assistance that changes them. State how those changes may affect later permissions and how that arrangement can be reviewed.
agent: Do not equate influence with illegitimacy. Bind formation purpose, intervention classes, scope criteria, review triggers, and locally valid ratification procedures when conditional authority depends on human-state signals.

name: Evaluate what remains after help
human: Evaluate present usefulness alongside transfer, recovery, correction, and the dependencies created. Account for the people who did not choose the system.
agent: Measure assisted success, transfer capacity, alternatives, review burden, and shared-resource effects separately. Treat access needs and chosen dependence explicitly. Keep artificial welfare uncertainty analytically distinct.
